title: Rover Farthest Reach Among Rocks
statement:
A rover starts at (0, 0) on an endless grid, facing north (the +y direction). It runs a list of commands:

  • -2: turn left 90 degrees.
  • -1: turn right 90 degrees.
  • 1 to 9: drive that many unit steps forward, one step at a time.

Some grid points hold rocks, listed in obstacles as [x, y]. If the next step would land on a rock, the rover stays where it is and skips the rest of that drive command, then continues with the next command. No rock sits on (0, 0).

Return the largest squared distance from the origin, x² + y², that the rover reaches at any moment.

examples.why: North to (0, 3), turn right, east to (2, 3), turn left, north to (2, 4). 2² + 4² = 20.
The rock at (0, 3) stops the rover at (0, 2) for the rest of the command.
The rover ends back at the origin, but it was 4 away at (0, 4). The answer is the farthest point on the way, not the end.

hints: Keep the direction as an index into a list of four (dx, dy) vectors. A right turn moves forward in the list, a left turn backward.
Drive one step at a time so you notice a rock in the middle of a command.
Checking every rock on every step is too slow. Put the rocks in a hash set keyed by their coordinates.

explain.intuition:
This is a straight simulation; the only real decision is how to ask "is there a rock here?" quickly. With up to 90 000 single steps and 10 000 rocks, scanning the rock list each step is too slow. A hash set of encoded coordinates answers each question in O(1).

Directions are easiest as an array [N, E, S, W] of (dx, dy) pairs. Turning right is +1 mod 4, turning left is +3 mod 4. Track the best squared distance after every step, because the rover can wander back toward the origin later.
steps: Store each rock as a key like "x,y" (or a single number) in a set.
For a drive command k, repeat up to k times: if the next cell is a rock, stop this command; otherwise move there and update best with x² + y².
pitfalls: Returning the distance at the end of the run instead of the maximum along the way.
Mixing up left and right. With the order N, E, S, W, a right turn is +1.
Stopping the whole program at a rock. Only the current drive command ends early.

solutions.title: Scan the rock list on every step
solutions.idea: Simulate exactly as described and check the next cell against every rock.

solutions.title: Hash set of rocks
solutions.idea: Same simulation, but rocks live in a set so each step checks its target cell in O(1).

followups: Drive commands can be up to 10⁹ steps. How would you jump straight to the first rock in the way?
The grid wraps around like a torus. What changes?
